top_categories.workout_context: 62 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Race-pace efforts that mimic VeloCity Berlin's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
VeloCity Berlin's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 62 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
VeloCity Berlin's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Base fitness for VeloCity Berlin. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of VeloCity Berlin. Train it until it feels boring.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At VeloCity Berlin, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
At VeloCity Berlin, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what VeloCity Berlin's mixed terrain actually does to you.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mixed terrain at tempo for 62 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.

race_overlay.heat: August in Berlin, Germany can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before VeloCity Berlin and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for VeloCity Berlin’s 62 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 62 miles of mixed terrain in Berlin, Germany.
